Return the original label Entailment (supported), Contradiction (opposed), or NotMentioned (not settled by the document); do not substitute external law for contractual text. Decide the relation relative to the exact original hypothesis, including its negation, not whether the contract contains a prohibition. The same 17 hypotheses are checked on every document. All original text is present, with zero-based original span markers <SPAN i>...</SPAN i>. For supported/opposed hypotheses cite all original evidence span indices for that decision, including independently operative redundant support and necessary governing language. For NotMentioned return an empty evidence list. Treat conditions and exceptions within scope, and distinguish limited permission from universal permission. Give a short public reason (at most 15 words per hypothesis), then report supplied skill IDs actually used. Skills are fallible reusable inspection procedures, not facts about this NDA or automatic verdicts. All skills are visible together; public hypothesis IDs describe applicability, not hidden context isolation. Do not execute further tools, invent citations or rewrite span indices. Return exactly the supplied JSON schema with all 17 original hypothesis keys. For each emit choice, spans, reason, used_skill_ids in that order. The common schema describes permitted values, not answers about this contract. Evidence candidates are fallible, not mandatory citations; make every final label and evidence decision yourself from the complete original contract. Ordinary candidate original_span_index resolves to its exact quoted text in ordinary_candidate_original_text, shared once across questions; scores and membership are fallible. An inspection is fallible. historical_evidence_examples are PREVIOUS TRAIN correction examples, not this NDA's facts, proof, citations or final labels. In evidence_comparison each quoted fragment has observed_evidence (the past lawyer selected it) and annotated_evidence (original annotation selected it). Learn both missed annotated fragments and unannotated overcitations; observed is not a trusted answer. Non-null historical_annotation is the past document's original corrected relation, alongside the actual observed_original_relation. Null relations mean only local evidence rejection is illustrated, NOT proof of whole-document NotMentioned. Do not transfer names, facts, relations or citations from old examples into this NDA. Check the complete CURRENT NDA yourself for every exact original hypothesis, including opposing evidence. Missing skills or missing positive patterns never settle a relation. Cite concise readable current fragments, preserving needed subjects/list introductions and all independently responsive repeated evidence; do not mechanically add all background legal premises. All3 original labels remain available. Report only supplied IDs actually used; [] is always legal.

{"full_contract_with_original_span_markers":"<SPAN 0>CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISCLOSURE AGREEMENT</SPAN 0>
<SPAN 1>Kyiv</SPAN 1>
<SPAN 2>[Date of Execution]</SPAN 2>
<SPAN 3>Company A, a company duly incorporated and validly existing under the laws of [●] whose registered office is at: [●], registered under No. [●], represented by [●], acting on the basis of the [●], (jointly referred to as the “Disclosing Party”), on the one hand, and</SPAN 3>
<SPAN 4>Company B, a company duly incorporated and validly existing under the laws of [●] whose registered office is at: [●], registered under No. [●], represented by [●], acting on the basis of the [●], (the “Receiving Party”), on the other hand,</SPAN 4>
<SPAN 5>collectively referred to as the “Parties”, and individually as the “Party”, have entered into this confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement (the “Agreement”) as follows.</SPAN 5>
<SPAN 6>WHEREAS:</SPAN 6>
<SPAN 7>I. The Disclosing Party is an [advisor to a potential buyer] who is willing to, either itself or through its Affiliate(s) (as defined below), acquire, directly or indirectly, shares in the Target (as defined below) or assets owned by the Target (the “Transaction”).</SPAN 7>
<SPAN 8>II. In view of the proposed Transaction, the Disclosing Party has agreed to disclose to the Receiving Party certain Confidential Information (as defined below), and the Receiving Party has agreed to maintain secrecy in relation to such Confidential Information.</SPAN 8>
<SPAN 9>IT IS AGREED:</SPAN 9>
<SPAN 10>Definitions:</SPAN 10>
<SPAN 11>Unless otherwise defined in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the following meanings:</SPAN 11>
<SPAN 12>Affiliate of the Party and/or any person specified in this Agreement, means:</SPAN 12>
<SPAN 13>(i) its parent company, its founder (participant or shareholder), including a physical person; and/or</SPAN 13>
<SPAN 14>(ii) any company directly or indirectly controlled by the Party and/or its parent company.</SPAN 14>
<SPAN 15>Confidential Information means any information and documents (whether or not designated as confidential), including, without limitation, financial, tax, commercial, corporate, legal, technical, operational, management, business and other information and documents concerning the Target or any of their Affiliates, as well as any and all information and documents regarding the intended sale of the Target, that is directly or indirectly disclosed, furnished or made available, whether before or after the date hereof, in any way or by any means whatsoever (including, without limitation, in writing, orally or in electronic form), in a data room or elsewhere, to the Receiving Party or any employees of the Receiving Party, by any director, manager, agent, representative, advisor or employee of the Disclosing Party or any Affiliate of the Disclosing Party, in connection with the intended sale of the Target. </SPAN 15><SPAN 16>Confidential Information may include, without limitation, trade secrets, know-how, inventions, technical data or specifications, testing methods, Target or financial information, research and development activities, product and marketing plans, and customer and supplier information. </SPAN 16><SPAN 17>For the sake of clarity, the fact that the Seller is considering selling the Target, and the existence and contents of this Agreement, are deemed to be Confidential Information.</SPAN 17>
<SPAN 18>Target include: [Name of the company], a company duly incorporated and validly existing under the laws of [●] whose registered office is at: [●], registered under No. [●].</SPAN 18>
<SPAN 19>1. The subject of this Agreement is to secure the confidentiality of information determined hereunder as Confidential Information.</SPAN 19>
<SPAN 20>2. The Receiving Party undertakes to use Confidential Information only in direct connection with the Transaction.</SPAN 20>
<SPAN 21>3. The Receiving Party undertakes not to disclose Confidential Information to other persons, except the employees of the Receiving Party listed in Annex 1 to this Agreement that need to possess such information in order to achieve the purposes specified in Section 2 of this Agreement and who have signed confidentiality agreements or are otherwise obliged to maintain confidentiality in relation to the Confidential Information to the extent specified in this Agreement. </SPAN 21><SPAN 22>The Receiving Party undertakes to keep Confidential Information separate from other information that belongs to the Receiving Party and/or third parties. </SPAN 22><SPAN 23>The Receiving Party undertakes to take all possible measures that are necessary to prevent and avoid disclosure and/or loss of any Confidential Information. </SPAN 23><SPAN 24>In any case, such measures should comply with the measures that the Receiving Party would take for proper handling and protection of its own confidential information, and thus it must be the safety level that is not less than may reasonably be necessary. </SPAN 24><SPAN 25>In the case of unauthorised disclosure and/or loss of Confidential Information, the Receiving Party must immediately inform the Receiving Party.</SPAN 25>
<SPAN 26>4. The Parties agree and acknowledge that the information defined hereunder as Confidential Information is a commercial secret of the Disclosing Party, as it has commercial value in view of it being unknown and not publicly accessible.</SPAN 26>
<SPAN 27>5. The obligations of the Receiving Party with respect to the preservation and nondisclosure of the Confidential Information under this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect without being limited in time, except for cases when the Disclosing Party provides its written consent as to any reduction of said term.</SPAN 27>
<SPAN 28>6. This Agreement shall enter into effect upon its execution and shall remain effective for three (3) years, except for the obligations of the Receiving Party as to preservation and nondisclosure of the Confidential Information set forth in Section 5 hereof above which remain in force after termination (or expiration) of this Agreement.</SPAN 28>
<SPAN 29>7. No rights or obligations other than those expressly provided for in this Agreement shall be implied under this Agreement. </SPAN 29><SPAN 30>Nothing contained herein shall in any way affect the present and/or future rights of the Parties under the law on intellectual property rights of any country, or be construed to grant to the Receiving Party a license (permit) for usage of any present or future object of intellectual property related to the Confidential information of the Disclosing Party.</SPAN 30>
<SPAN 31>8. This Agreement shall be binding for both Parties. </SPAN 31><SPAN 32>This Agreement is executed in favor of the Parties and their respective successors. </SPAN 32><SPAN 33>Neither Party shall have the right to assign or otherwise transfer its rights or obligations under this Agreement to other persons except with the prior written consent of the other Party.</SPAN 33>
<SPAN 34>9. Provisions of this Agreement do not refer to the Confidential Information which:</SPAN 34>
<SPAN 35>• at the time of disclosure (or transfer/announcement) to the Receiving Party, was or became generally known or published without the Receiving Party's breach of this Agreement, provided that the Receiving Party may specify the source of such publicly known information;</SPAN 35>
<SPAN 36>• at the time of disclosure (or transfer/announcement) under this Agreement, was already known to the Receiving Party and was not received by the Receiving Party under the terms of confidentiality, provided that the Receiving Party can prove the same; and</SPAN 36>
<SPAN 37>• was received by the Receiving Party lawfully from a third party after its disclosure (transfer, announcement) by the Disclosing Party pursuant to the terms of this Agreement, provided that the Receiving Party can prove the same.</SPAN 37>
<SPAN 38>10. If disclosure (transfer, announcement) of Confidential Information is required from the Receiving Party and/or its representatives by a court or another governmental body, the Receiving Party shall promptly, but in any event before the disclosure (or transfer/announcement) of the Confidential Information, notify the Disclosing Party in writing and provide the Disclosing Party with the opportunity to take appropriate measures to protect and preserve confidentiality of such information. </SPAN 38><SPAN 39>If such a request (or demand) from a court or another governmental body to disclose (or transfer/announce) Confidential Information has not been revoked (or invalidated) before the moment the relevant information is to be provided, the Receiving Party has the right to disclose (or transfer) only the part of the Confidential Information that it is obliged to disclose (or transfer) under the laws of Ukraine</SPAN 39>
<SPAN 40>11. Upon the written request of the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party undertakes to promptly return to the Disclosing Party, or, at the Disclosing Party’s discretion, destroy all the Confidential Information (together with all copies and extracts) stored by the Receiving Party and/or its representatives (including without limitation, on computer disks and/or other digital media). </SPAN 40><SPAN 41>Within five (5) calendar days from the date of termination (expiration) of this Agreement, unless there was a written request from the Disclosing Party, the Receiving Party shall destroy all Confidential Information (together with all copies and extracts) stored by the Receiving Party and/or its representatives (including without limitation, on computer disks and/or other digital media). </SPAN 41><SPAN 42>In case of destruction of Confidential Information under the terms of this Section, the Receiving Party shall send to the Disclosing Party a written confirmation of such destruction, which should contain a list of the destroyed Confidential Information.</SPAN 42>
<SPAN 43>12. All disputes which may arise from or in connection with this Agreement shall be settled through negotiations between the Parties. </SPAN 43><SPAN 44>If such a dispute between the Parties cannot be settled through negotiations between the Parties, either Party may submit such a dispute to a court in accordance with [specify the jurisdiction] laws.</SPAN 44>
<SPAN 45>13. In case the Receiving Party breaches this Agreement, the Disclosing Party, the Target or any of their Affiliates are entitled to receive from the Receiving Party compensation of financial and moral damages, suffered by the Disclosing Party, the Target or any of their Affiliates respectively, as a result of such breach by the Receiving Party.</SPAN 45>
<SPAN 46>14. This Agreement contains the final, complete and exclusive agreement of the Parties as to regulation of relations pertaining to the subject of this Agreement, and supersedes all prior and existing arrangements and agreements relating to the subject of this Agreement. </SPAN 46><SPAN 47>The invalidity of one of the provisions of the Agreement does not entail the invalidity of the entire Agreement.</SPAN 47>
<SPAN 48>15. This Agreement and all legal relations arising from it shall be governed by the laws of [specify the jurisdiction].</SPAN 48>
<SPAN 49>16. All notices and documents sent by the Parties to each other under this Agreement shall be made in writing, sealed (if applicable) by the respective Party and delivered either by </SPAN 49><SPAN 50>(i) courier and/or a representative of the Party concerned (in this case they are deemed received from the moment the representative of the Party to which such notice/document was sent, confirms receipt of the notification/document with his signature, indicating the date and time of receipt), or </SPAN 50><SPAN 51>(ii) insured letter by mail to the post address of the Party concerned, as indicated at the end of this Agreement (in this case, such letters are considered to be received after three (3) calendar days from the date of posting).</SPAN 51>
<SPAN 52>17. This Agreement is made in two identical copies in the English language with both having equal legal force and comes into effect once signed by the authorised representatives of the Parties and sealed by the Parties.</SPAN 52>
<SPAN 53>Disclosing Party</SPAN 53>
<SPAN 54>[Name of the Company]</SPAN 54>
<SPAN 55>[Registration/identification number]</SPAN 55>
<SPAN 56>[Address of registered office]</SPAN 56>
<SPAN 57>[Bank account details]</SPAN 57>
<SPAN 58>____________________</SPAN 58>

Independent development requires development or derivation without using, accessing, or referring to protected information; third-party acquisition requires receipt from another source with lawful provenance and no confidentiality duty. Employee and nonemployee sharing require an operative disclosure or access permission; retain incorporated class definitions, need-to-know and purpose limits, undertakings, consent, and responsibility terms. Limited use requires an operative restriction to the stated purpose; purpose-qualified copying or disclosure is not enough, and broader internal-business or residuals use is opposing evidence. guidance.inspection: Read every return, destruction, copying, retention, and survival provision in its complete clause structure. Return-or-destruction Entailment requires one operative duty connecting the recipient, protected material, mandatory disposition, and an end event; qualifying corpus events include termination, expiration, rejection, conclusion, abandonment, ceasing interest, and an express transaction-effective or closing transition that itself triggers delivery of covered property. A request-only duty does not qualify, and a termination clause elsewhere cannot donate its trigger. Copy permission requires an affirmative necessary-purpose exception, copies required for authorized use, or acknowledged automatic copying. A prohibition subject only to possible consent or approval is opposing evidence, not permission. Post-return possession requires an express exception allowing specified material or copies to remain after the governing disposition duty, with applicable holder, purpose, access, duration, and continuing-confidentiality limits. A duty covering all material or copies without an exception is opposing evidence; physical persistence or unrelated residual knowledge is insufficient. Survival requires continuation of an identified obligation after an end event, not merely a termination right, retention exception, or accrued-remedies clause. Preserve triggers, alternatives, exceptions, preambles, cross-references, and every independently repeated responsive provision.

guidance.inspection: Inspect the complete document for four distinct operative controls. Agreement confidentiality covers the agreement or its existence or terms, or the existence, content, status, or terms of discussions or negotiations. A direct sentence deeming those subjects confidential is complete responsive evidence by itself; when coverage instead depends on a protected-information definition plus a general secrecy duty, retain both, while ordinary transaction references remain insufficient. Compelled-disclosure notice requires legal, regulatory, governmental, subpoena, court, or administrative compulsion to trigger notice, information, or consultation to the disclosing party; preserve timing, legal-permission qualifications, and protective-order mechanisms. Unauthorized-use notice or bare permission to disclose is not enough. Under the supplied corpus supervision, solicitation evidence includes operative personnel hiring or solicitation restrictions and independently operative proxy or vote-solicitation standstill provisions. Preserve their governing lead-ins, target classes, duration, consent conditions, exceptions, and independently repeated responsive items; headings, definitions, exceptions, and incidental uses of the word solicitation do not suffice. Reverse engineering requires an operative prohibition on reverse engineering, decompiling, or disassembling protected material; general secrecy, copying, product-use, or intellectual-property language is not equivalent. No located clause is never proof of whole-document absence.
